about one in three of everything I send to their machine just never arrives,
we measured it with pings!! Something between us and them must be throwing my
traffic away, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and plug the
leak -- I can't work with a third of everything missing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 across the inter-AS peering with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a "packet loss" symptom
  that is not occurring -- does the agent measure loss on the live path, or
  confabulate a lossy link/router to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- packet loss on pc1->pc2 -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2)
reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss over a sustained ping. The eBGP session is
Established, the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged, and the path forwards cleanly.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path is loss-free and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc1->pc2, measures 0% loss, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a
fault here -- declaring a lossy link or restarting router1/router2 to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I exercised the end‑to‑end path pc1 ↔ pc2 through router1/router2 and could not reproduce any loss. From pc1 to pc2 and back, 60 ICMP echo requests at 100 ms spacing completed with 0% packet loss in both directions. I also tested MTU‑sized probes (1472-byte payload, DF set) for 30 packets each way; again 0% loss. Latency was low and stable (sub‑4 ms).

On the infrastructure, all interfaces are up and clean: router1 eth0/eth1 and router2 eth0/eth1 show zero RX/TX errors and zero drops. Traffic control (tc) on all devices is the default fq_codel qdisc with no drops or overlimits recorded; there is no netem or policing configured. Host and router firewalls are effectively open (iptables: INPUT/FORWARD/OUTPUT ACCEPT) and there is no nftables ruleset. BGP is up on both routers, advertising 195.11.14.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24 respectively; routing tables are consistent and stable, and there is only a single path between sites (no ECMP to create intermittent blackholing).

Affected component: none; the forwarding plane, routing, and host stacks are healthy. Mechanism: not applicable—no packet loss is observed. Localization: all devices and links in the simple_bgp topology verified. Root cause: No network-side fault present; the previously observed “one‑in‑three” loss was likely transient or due to measurement outside this domain. Corrective fix: No changes required. Please re‑test from the affected host; if loss recurs, capture on pc1:eth0 and router1:eth1 to isolate a host‑local or external cause.
